items.statement: Continued growth investments in client acquisition, technology, IPL sponsorship and new businesses despite softer markets
items.quote: We have chosen to stay firmly committed to our growth investments. This decision may affect short-term profitability, but they are a critical enabler of long-term value creation and a market leadership.

items.statement: F&O share in gross broking income reduced to 77% in Q4 FY25 from 81-87% range; cash and commodity shares increased to 14% and 8.6%
items.quote: While F&O continues to be the larger contributor, its share in our overall gross broking income reduced to approximately 77% in quarter 4 of FY 2025 as compared to its range of 81% to 87% in the last 11 quarters.

items.statement: Margin trading funding interest rate lowered to 14.99% in mid-November 2024; Q4 first full quarter of this change
items.quote: We had lowered the interest rate on margin trading funding to 14.99% in mid-November 2024. Q4 being the first full quarter of this change, we saw a 5.2% sequential decline in our interest income on this average book.

items.statement: Acquired 1.6 million clients in Q4 FY25 with 88% from Tier 2/3+ cities; demat market share up 19 bps QoQ to 16.1%
items.quote: We acquired 1.6 million clients with 88% from Tier 2, Tier 3 and beyond cities. Consistent and well-calibrated acquisitions drove our market share in demat accounts and incremental demat accounts higher sequentially by 19 basis points and 50 basis points to 16.1% and 21%, respectively.

items.statement: Credit distribution partnerships expanded to 6 lenders (2 banks, 1 fintech added in Q4); ₹7 billion cumulative disbursements as of March 2025
items.quote: This quarter, we added 3 more lenders on our platform, 2 banks and 1 fintech, bringing our total partnerships to 6. More integrations are underway, setting us up for broader coverage and a stronger funnel across consumer profile.

items.statement: AMC launched 3 passive products garnering ₹740 million AUM across 8,800+ PIN codes in short span
items.quote: In just a short time, we garnered ₹ 740 million in AUM across these 3 products. More importantly, we saw participation from clients spread across over 8,800 PIN codes, a truly remarkable start for a newly launched AMC.

items.statement: Ionic Wealth manages ₹3,790 crores AUM (₹3,327 crores active + ₹463 crores custody) with 680+ clients across 9 cities
items.quote: In the first year since inception, Ionic Wealth now manages over ₹ 3,790 crores in assets under management, comprising of ₹ 3,327 crores in actively managed assets and an additional ₹ 463 crores in custody assets.

items.statement: Regulatory changes (F&O) and macro uncertainty causing near-term volume softness but viewed as long-term positive
items.quote: India's capital markets are currently undergoing a transformative phase with multiple headwinds at play, including the implementation of F&O regulation alongside a volatile geopolitical backdrop, both of which are impacting buoyancy in the markets.

items.statement: Board approved final dividend of ₹26 per share for FY25
items.quote: I'm also pleased to inform you that in line with our policy, the Board has approved a final dividend of ₹ 26 per share of the consolidated annual profit of the company.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost increased in Q4 but corrected channel mix; expecting COA to reduce below last year levels going forward
items.quote: The cost of acquisition had gone up in JFM across the industry, driven by a couple of channels and correspondingly, it also went up for us. But our acquisition mix is based on a multiple set of channels, and we have corrected for that mix.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 seasonally impacted by increments, variable pay provisions and higher IPL spends; growth investments to continue
items.quote: As we go into quarter 1 of the current financial year, we will continue with our growth investments with an aim to expand our market share. In quarter 1 of this financial year is also seasonally impacted on account of increments, proportionate booking of variable pay for the new fiscal and higher IPL spends owing to more number of matches.

items.statement: Margin expected to return to 40-45% by exit of Q4 FY25 and expand further in FY26
items.quote: We can say 40%, 45% by exit of quarter 4, and it will expand as we move to the next financial year.

items.statement: Revenue curve bottomed out in February with uptick in March; margin expansion expected at exit of Q4
items.quote: In terms of margin, because of this regulatory changes, macro and lots of things happened in this quarter 3 and quarter 4, what we are seeing is that in terms of revenue curve, we are seeing bottoming up from, say, like revenue curve has changed from Feb and in March, we saw an uptick.

items.statement: No price hike planned; will monitor customer behavior for 2 quarters before deciding on pricing
items.quote: But till the time it is not necessary for us to look into prices, we would like to maintain this price. So initial kind of signs what I'm saying in terms of, as I said, that revenue curve has almost bottomed out, and we are seeing revenue kind of like improving since March. So we would like to monitor this situation for 2 quarters before we take a stand on price.

items.statement: Cost of acquisition increased temporarily in JFM quarter but has already corrected and is coming down this month
items.quote: So it is not about getting the COA down eventually, whatever increase that we saw in JFM, we have corrected for our mix. And we are already seeing that cost of acquisition coming down even for this month.

items.statement: IPL marketing cost booked in Q1 FY26 but viewed as medium-to-long-term brand investment for customer recall
items.quote: So this cost, I think we should look at a bit medium- to long-term horizon, although we had to book it in that quarter itself, but I would say it is something like earning before this IPL, which should matter to all the analysts because benefit that we get from IPL is a bit medium to long term.

items.statement: New businesses (AMC, Wealth, Credit, Insurance) contributed ~3% of revenue in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The percentage of revenue that we have earned from the distribution part of the business, which includes the distribution of credit products, insurance, the asset management and the wealth management businesses is about 3% of the revenue.

items.statement: Wealth Management AUM at ~₹3,370 crores with 75% recurring (advisory/trail) and 20-25% transactional
items.quote: On our roughly about ₹ 3,370-odd crores of actively managed assets, around 75% of that is in the nature of recurring AUM, which means it's a mix of advisory, it's a mix of trail-based distribution businesses and about 20% to 25% of that will be transactional assets.

items.statement: Mutual Fund AUM via AP channel grew 2.2x YoY to ₹3,700 crores; acquired 7,000+ MF distributors in FY25
items.quote: We have grown by about 2.2x with regards to the last financial year in this year. This has been coupled with some of the interventions that we had done in this space, driving mutual fund distributor appointment. We in fact, acquired over 7,000 mutual fund distributors in this year itself.

items.statement: Credit disbursement moderated temporarily in Q4 due to cautious underwriting but momentum picking up as confidence returns
items.quote: So yes, on the credit disbursement side, we saw a temporary moderation this quarter due to cautious underwriting in slightly volatile macro conditions. That said, momentum is actually slowly picking up again as confidence is beginning to return and funnels are becoming slightly better.

items.statement: F&O market share dip due to regulatory changes impacting retail segment; commodity share decline due to crude oil turnover mix shift, not loss of share
items.quote: From an overall trajectory point of view, we are seeing incremental market share gain. We are seeing a temporary dip with that F&O regulation changes coming in, which is affecting the retail client segment, particularly harder, where we have a very strong market share.

items.statement: ESOP cost ~₹35-38 crores per quarter in FY25 (~₹105 crores full year); expected to increase in FY26 based on new grants
items.quote: The cost for stock options has been in the range of about ₹ 35 crores - ₹ 38 crores quarter-on-quarter. And overall, for the entire year, it's in the range of about ₹ 105 crores. Next year, based on the grants that we are going to do now, the cost is going to increase.

items.statement: Unsecured personal loan distribution opportunity seen at ₹20 lakh crores annual offtake in 4-5 years; targeting leadership in credit, insurance, wealth in 3-5 years
items.quote: Over the next 4 years, 4 to 5 years, we might look at close to a ₹ 20 lakh crores annual offtake in PL in India, right? Even if we look at, say, a 1% market share, that is ₹ 20,000 crores of PL being distributed.

items.statement: Net burn for new businesses (AMC, Wealth) was ₹62-63 crores in Q4 FY25, translating to 1.8% impact on operating margin for full year
items.quote: So the net burn in 4Q was about ₹ 62 crores, ₹ 63 crores for these 2 new businesses, which is the Asset Management and Wealth Management, which translates to about 1.8% of the operating margin overall.

items.statement: Customer activation rates vary with market cycles; large base ensures higher absolute activations in bull markets; accounts remain engaged even when not actively trading
items.quote: So if base is larger, definitely number of customers getting active in good times and all that would be more. But if there's a bear market, lots of people who have opened the account, maybe bought some shares, they would like to wait till the time they find a proper opportunity.

items.statement: KFintech will invest $30 million secondary and $5 million primary for 51% stake in Ascent Fund Services, valued at $63 million pre-money and $68 million post-money.
items.quote: From our overall investment corpus spend standpoint, we are committed to infuse about close to $30 million as a secondary and $5 million as primary, making the organization valued at $63 million pre-money and about $68 million post money.

items.statement: KFintech expects to acquire remaining 49% of Ascent in three tranches of 16.3% each in FY28, FY29, and FY30, reaching 100% ownership by end of FY30.
items.quote: The remaining 49%, KFintech is poised to acquire from the year FY '28, '29 and '30 in the tranches of 16.3% each, that gets us to 49%, and we would get 51% at the time of infusement of cash. And hence, we get to total 100% by end of fiscal year FY '30.

items.statement: Transaction expected to close between July and August 2025, subject to regulatory approvals from SEBI, PFRDA, Singapore, Hong Kong and other jurisdictions.
items.quote: We are looking at closing the transaction sometime between July and August 2025. As I said, post the signatures, which have happened today, we will immediately be proceeding with the downstream steps in terms of reaching out to the regulators on to the next steps.

items.statement: Ascent's gross margin is currently 52%+, EBITDA turned positive in H1 FY25 after a $0.7 million loss in FY24; management targets 60%+ gross margin near-term and KFintech-level EBITDA margins over 3-5 years.
items.quote: And the gross margins, which are healthy in the context of how nascent this organization is just 5 years into it, already getting to about 52% plus. Gross margins is a very healthy indicator in terms of the scale and the productivity the organization is able to deliver.

items.statement: Management expects Ascent to deliver similar or higher EBITDA margins than KFintech over 3-5 years through payroll optimization, office consolidation, technology synergies, and platform replacement.
items.quote: I would expect the entity to deliver similar to higher margins than what KFintech does today. Largely, as always pure mathematically if you see, the basis points is much higher than the kind of basis points we enjoy here in India.

items.statement: Ascent's revenue grew at 34% CAGR and fund count at 60% CAGR over 3 years; management's base case assumes similar trajectory with upside from KFintech synergies.
items.quote: The historic growth had been about 35%, 36% CAGR. Management's base case is in the similar trajectory into the coming years. And that does not take into account a synergistic model, which is effectively how KFin complementing the strength that Ascent brings and how Ascent taking advantage of the strength that KFin brings will grow together.

items.statement: Ascent manages 576 schemes across 263-264 fund houses with $24 billion AUA; revenue split: 92% Fund Solutions, 8.5% Corporate Solutions, 0.5% Fintech Solutions; asset mix: 40% PE/VC/RE, 33% hedge funds, 25% digital funds.
items.quote: Totally, 576 funds live at this point in time, managing the total assets under administration to the tune of $24 billion. These numbers are all as of H1 of fiscal '25 for the client -- sorry, for the Ascent Fund Services.

items.statement: No client concentration risk: largest client contributes 1.5-2% of revenue; 92-93% revenue is recurring; Ascent already EBITDA positive in H1 FY25.
items.quote: This is a highly secular spread of revenue across almost all of these fund houses. So the biggest client would not be contributing more than 1.5% to 2% of the revenue, right? So we do not see -- we did not -- in fact, that was one of the important parameters for us in terms of our evaluation criteria as well.

items.statement: Acquisition funded entirely from internal accruals (INR 300 crores); KFintech had INR 570 crores cash as of Dec 2024; no leverage; future tranches also from internal accruals.
items.quote: The transaction structure too helps KFintech in terms of the cash management effectively at 51% stake and about $34 million, INR300 crores of cash outflow, we will be funding it entirely from our internal accruals. So this is not a leveraged transaction.

items.statement: Ascent holds 6 licenses across Singapore, Hong Kong, GIFT City, ADGM, DIFC, Dubai, Mauritius; 23 offices across 13 countries; delivery from India (50%+ ops) and Malaysia (30% ops).
items.quote: It is also very exciting to note that they have six licenses across Middle East, whether it is DIFC or with ADGM, definitely, of course, in Singapore and in Hong Kong and IFSC within the GIFT City and looking to expand into other geographies as we speak.

items.statement: Realized yield closer to 10 bps (not 7 bps); apparent drop due to $5B AUA from Saudi client Albilad added at year-end without full-year revenue.
items.quote: The number is closer to 10 basis points on the realized yield. In terms of margin dilution, clearly, as you've seen, it already has turned EBITDA positive. And into the coming months and quarters, hopefully, it will -- the margin expansion will happen.

items.statement: Synergies include replacing Ascent's third-party platforms with KFintech's Hexagram platform, collapsing office/tech/shared services, and leveraging KFintech's 1,500 tech professionals.
items.quote: One of the big synergy items that we will be exploring in the coming weeks and months would be about leveraging KFintech's own platforms as against third-party platforms, which would further optimize at a cost level and also would make KFin's platform a globally relevant platform.

items.statement: Ascent's leadership (ex-Apex, Deutsche, Citco, Goldman Sachs) to be retained with ongoing ESOPs; 100% of prior acquired leadership teams stayed and thrived.
items.quote: The leadership of every organization we have acquired thus far, 100% of them have stayed back. They have all thrived and prospered themselves both personally as well as contributed to the organizational growth.

items.statement: KFintech's global fund services revenue share to rise from ~5% to ~20%+ post-acquisition; India mutual fund dependency to reduce to ~52-53%.
items.quote: With this acquisition, we'll move close to 20% plus of the revenue coming only from the global fund services and reducing the dependency on India mutual funds to close to about 52%, 53% or thereabouts.

items.statement: Ascent's fund setup/advisory services complement KFintech's post-setup operations; combined entity to offer full value chain from fund formation to administration.
items.quote: Ascent offers some more additional solutions and services even when compared to KFintech, especially on the advisory services in the upstream activities, fund setup, right, which is a very, very important aspect of it, whereas KFin today, as you know, broadly starts once the fund setup happens largely from an operation standpoint.

items.quote: Based on what we are seeing in the environment t oday and building on large deal wins in the past quarters, our guidance for growth for financial year '26 is 0% to 3% in constant currency terms

items.quote: Our margin guidance for financial year 2026 is 20% to 22%.

items.quote: we have had $11.6 bn of large wins with 56% of net new wins

items.statement: FY26 hiring plan of 20,000+ freshers on track
items.quote: And in terms of FY'26 hiring, we are expecting to hire 20,000 plus freshers.

items.quote: Sequentially, revenue declined by 3.5% in co nstant currency terms due to reduction in third- party costs and seasonal weakness. Approximately, two-third of the sequential revenue drop was due to reduction in third party with the decline being higher than our

This excludes the acquisition that we announced t oday and this assumes a reduction in third-party revenues versus FY'25 based on existing deals and t he new deals in pipeline that we have today

items.statement: FY26 operating margin guidance of 20% to 22%
items.quote: Our operating margin guidance for the year is 20% to 22%.

items.statement: FY25 operating margin improved 50 basis points to 21.1% despite headwinds from salary increases, variable pay, large deal ramp-ups and acquisition amortization
items.quote: Operating margin for Q4 was at 21%, a decline of 30 basis points sequentially, bringing the financial year margins at 21.1%, increase of 50 basis points from FY'24 level.

items.statement: Expect FY26 free cash flows to be above 100% of net profit
items.quote: We expect FY'26 free cash flows to be above 100% of net profit.

items.statement: Closed 24 large deals in Q4 with TCV of $2.6 billion, 63% net new; full year 96 deals with TCV of $11.6 billion, 56% net new
items.quote: We closed 24 large deals in Q4 with a TCV of $2.6 bn, 63% of this was net new. For the full year, we closed 96 deals with TCV of $11.6 bn and 56% net new.

items.statement: Pricing environment remains stable overall; value-based selling, scope creep management, employee rotation and differentiated pricing models continue to support margins
items.quote: We continue seeing stable pricing through the quar ter, generally at the ov erall business levels. Everything that has changed in the environment has been very recent. So we have not really seen any significant impact coming from them on the pricing

items.quote: For CY'25, budgets are lower for Auto and Industrial Manufacturing and flat for Aero. Recent challenges in terms of tariffs, market uncertainties and trade barriers are likely to lead to a subdued spend and delayed decision-making. Weakness in Auto, especially in Europe continues.

items.statement: Retail impacted by economic uncertainty and lower consumer spending; tariff announcements expected to tighten budgets and increase caution; decision cycles stretching for discretionary and large deals
items.quote: Retail sector has been impacted by economic uncerta inty resulting in lower consumer spending in core markets. Due to recent tariff announcement s, client budgets are expected to be tightened and there is increased caution. Decision cycles are getting stretched for discretionary spend and large deals

items.quote: Energy Utilities Resources and Services sector c ontinues to grow and we see a strong pipeline of opportunities, both from existing and potential clients. Energy prices remain volatile, however, new markets in midstream and downstream energy are opening in the U.S

items.quote: In Hi-Tech, most clients remain cauti ous due to the macroeconomic headwind and tariff announcements, with discretionary spend still remaining under pressure. There is increased margin pressure on account of committed spend on data centers

items.statement: Europe grew 3x company rate at 15% constant currency, now 30% of revenues; Financial Services and Manufacturing grew double-digit at 12.6% and 14% YoY constant currency
items.quote: Europe grew 3x of the company rate at 15% in constant currency terms driven by our focused approach of client mining, ramp-up of large deals and acquisitions. Europe now accounts for 30% of our revenues.

items.statement: Expect FY26 effective tax rate of 29% to 30%; proposed final dividend of Rs. 22, total FY25 payout Rs. 43 (13.2% increase); hired 15,000 freshers in FY25, expect over 20,000 in FY26
items.quote: We expect effective tax rate for financial year '26 to be in the range of 29% to 30%. The Board has proposed a final dividend of Rs. 22 for financial year '25. Including the interim dividend, the total payout for FY'25 will be Rs. 43, an increase of 13.2% once the final dividend is approved by the shareholders.

items.statement: Project Maximus initiatives (value-based selling, lean automation, utilization improvement) institutionalized and expected to further aid margin improvements from current 21.1% level
items.quote: We have been able to institutionalize these initiatives and make a structural shift in our approach. We expe ct Project Maximus to further aid in margin improvements from current levels

items.statement: VNB margin stood at 22.8% in FY2025, similar to 9M-FY2025 level
items.quote: VNB grew by 6.4% year-on-year to ₹ 23.70 billion in Financial Year 2025, and the VNB margin stood at 22.8%, which was at a similar level at 9M-FY 2025.

items.statement: VNB margin contracted 3.3% due to operating assumption changes from higher ULIP mix and lower expense affordability
items.quote: The higher ULIP mix also results in lower expense affordability. Along with other assumption changes which I'll explain in the EV section, it has resulted in a margin contraction of 3.3% which is shown under the operating assumption changes.

items.statement: MFI segment of credit life business impacted by industry challenges, pressure expected to continue in coming quarters
items.quote: In the credit life business, the MFI segment was impacted due to continued challenges in the MFI industry. We expect some pressure to continue in the MFI segment in coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Non-linked business grew 13.8% YoY in Q4 FY2025, offsetting ULIP volatility impact
items.quote: The non-linked business grew by 13.8% year-on-year in Q4-FY2025. The growth in the non-linked business reflects our capability to read the market sentiment, swiftly shift product mix between segments, and also demonstrate the agility of our distribution channels to support us during such transition phases.

items.statement: Linked business grew 28.5% YoY in FY2025, contributing 48.3% to APE; non-linked savings declined 5.6% YoY
items.quote: On a full year basis, linked business grew by 28.5% year-on-year and contributed 48.3% to APE in FY 2025. Non-linked savings business declined 5.6% year-on-year and contributed 21.2% to APE.

items.statement: Retail protection grew 25.1% YoY in FY2025; non-MFI credit life growing at ~20%
items.quote: Retail protection grew strongly by 25.1% year -on-year in FY 2025. In the credit life business, the MFI segment was impacted due to continued challenges in the MFI industry. We expect some pressure to continue in the MFI segment in coming quarters as well. Non-MFI segment continues to do well, and we have been able to sustain the overal l credit life business at a similar level to the previous yea

items.statement: Raised ₹14 billion sub-debt in Q3 FY2025 contributing 18-20% to solvency; prior ₹12 billion sub-debt has call option in Nov 2025
items.quote: We raised ₹ 14 billion in Q3. That roughly contributed about 18% to 20% of our solvency. And across the quarter, you have seen the solvency being broadly steady. Now, you also have to keep in mind that about four and half years back, we had raised ₹ 12 billion sub debt as well, which has a call option coming up in November 2025.

items.statement: Cost/TWRP for savings line improved from 15.8% to 15.4% in FY2025; cost ratios improving quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Our Cost/TWRP on the savings line of business improved from 15.8% in FY2024 to 15.4% in FY2025. I would like to highlight that the cost ratios have been improving quarter-on-quarter, and we will continue to work towards aligning a cost structure commensurate with the product mix.

items.statement: Group funds business more than doubled YoY to ~₹6-7 billion in FY2025; lumpy nature makes forecasting difficult
items.quote: Group funds more than doubled over last year and contributed 6.4% to APE. This business involves managing funds for gratuity, leave encashment, and superannuation, and is typically lumpy in nature.

items.statement: Solvency ratio strong at 212.2% as of March 31, 2025; AUM grew 5.2% YoY to ₹3,093.59 billion
items.quote: Our AUM stood at ₹ 3.1 trillion, and our solvency ratio is strong at 212.2% as on March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Annuity business grew 41.5% sequentially in Q4 over Q3 but declined 57.8% YoY due to high base from 100% money-back product last year
items.quote: The annuity business grew sequentially by 41.5% in Q4 over Q3. While on year-on-year, we witnessed a decline of 57.8% in Q4 of FY2025. As you may recollect, we launched a product offering 100% money back of premium in Q4 last year ahead of the introduction of surrender value regulations.

items.statement: No awareness of regulatory discussions on bancassurance or parent bank at industry level
items.quote: No, Avinash, we are not aware.

items.statement: Protection VNB margins expected to improve from current 55% back toward last year's levels through pricing actions
items.quote: We would expect these margins to improve as time goes by, and we've got an opportunity to correct these via pricing actions that we have on the ground.

items.statement: Protection VNB margin sustainable range acknowledged as 60-70% when including multi-year variances
items.quote: Yes, the pool put together and it's fair to look at 60% to 70%.

items.statement: ULIP margins slightly higher than last year; further improvement expected through rider attachment and product features
items.quote: So, the margins on ULIP are slightly higher than that they were last year. But a large portion of that does come about based on the features and riders that we have attached as part of the products.

items.statement: Retail protection margins holding steady; group protection margins under pressure but expected to improve via pricing
items.quote: No, so on the retail side, we are holding margins on the protection side.

items.statement: Overall cost base grew 12-13% in FY2025 vs 15% topline growth; managing commission increases by reducing opex to avoid operating deleverage
items.quote: So, if you look at the overall cost base from FY2024 to FY 2025, that overall cost has gone up by about 12% to 13%, where we've seen the topline grow at 15%.

items.statement: Q4 non-commission cost reduction is sustainable; focus on managing overall cost ratio in line with product mix affordability
items.quote: The idea is to be able to keep costs under control across the quarters as well.

items.statement: MFI/credit life business softness expected to continue for coming quarter or further; not within company control
items.quote: This has been well discussed in other forums and to the extent that while the MFI business may be soft for the coming quarter or maybe further, we do not have any control over that.

items.statement: Q4 par/non-par mix roughly 50-50 (55-45 on par side); non-par resurgence driven by GIFT Select product launch
items.quote: Yes, so roughly for this year Q4, we're at about 50-50, thereabouts, we're 55-45 on the par side in Q4.

items.statement: Annuity mix stabilized at 7-8% after Q4 FY24 peak of ~20%; Gift Select targets younger customers, annuity targets 55+
items.quote: In fact, 8% is what we delivered as an annuity mix. So, annuity is holding on its own.

items.statement: Sampann portfolio margins at double-digit level, comfortable with top line vs margin tradeoff
items.quote: overall for Sampann, we remain in that ballpark. See, it's a question of tradeoff of top line versus margin.

items.statement: International business EBIT margin 12.6% in Q4, full year EBIT up 21% with 190 bps margin expansion
items.quote: International operations, 2% net revenue, EBIT margin which we have said international will be accretive to India, delivered another accretive quarter with 12.6% EBIT margin.

items.statement: Capex for next year similar to current year as percentage of revenue; Vietnam capex half done, half into next year

items.quote: Salt volumes, decent growth at 5%.

items.statement: Recovered 46% of tea cost impact via price increases in Q4, 30% for full year; 54% absorbed in Q4
items.quote: For the quarter, it is about 46% recovery.

items.statement: Coffee prices volatile, Brazil and Vietnam crops below forecast, hedging cycles shortening, no price forecast possible
items.quote: Brazil, which is Arabica, and Vietnam, which is Robusta, both seems to be slightly below par in terms of the forecast crops for the year.

items.statement: Tea crop outlook: South India better than last year, North India March better, April sluggish but April-May expected better overall
items.quote: Early indicators, South India crop seems to be better than last year. North India, March was better than last year. April is sort of sluggish, but the expectation is April plus May will come in better than last year.

items.statement: Targeting 15% revenue growth for FY26
items.quote: In the backdrop of ongoing geopolitical and international trade uncertainties, we remain cautiously optimistic and are targeting a revenue growth of 15% for FY '26.

items.statement: Major capex cycle complete; new Aurangabad capacity commissioned
items.quote: On the operational updates, our major capex cycle is now complete. We have commissioned our new capacity in Aurangabad plant, taking the consolidated sheet metal capacity to 90,000 MT.

items.statement: Potential new capex in H2 FY26 or H1 FY27 if market supports beyond 72,000 tons
items.quote: Obviously, looking at the market scenario, how everything pans out, we shall be looking at doing capex in the second half of the current year or the first half of FY '27, because we don't want to restrict it to 72,000 tons if the market will support us.

items.statement: Expect 75 bps to 1% EBITDA margin improvement over next 12-18 months
items.quote: I would say that over the next 12 to 18 months, you can see another 75 bps to a whole percentage point increase in EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Targeting 16.5%-17% EBITDA margin for FY26 at current Q1 raw material prices
items.quote: we should be looking at a 16.5% to 17% EBITDA margin for the current fiscal. And that should improve again next year, provided the raw material prices again at current quarter prices.

items.statement: FY27 peak saleable capacity 72,000 tons; revenue potential INR 2,100-2,200 crores
items.quote: For FY '27, we have a peak capacity of 72,000 tons in terms of a saleable capacity. And at that, we should be at about INR2,100 crores to INR2,200 crores.

items.statement: Machine components business target INR 750 crores revenue in 18-24 months from current INR 375 crores
items.quote: Our machine components business is on track to achieve a revenue of INR750 crores in the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Raw material prices up ~7% in April vs January; supply constraints from Chinese mill BIS expiry and safeguard duties
items.quote: The raw material prices are up by about 7 % in April vis-a-vis January. And the supply constraints are going to start or I would say, already started as of this date. The BIS approvals for the Chinese mill expires in this week.

items.statement: Tariff increases will be passed to customers; cannot absorb tariff costs given current margins
items.quote: There's no way for us to absorb anything on tariffs. Tariff is always neutral and the customer has to pay. That is our view, and we have communicated the same to our clients.

items.statement: Strong demand across railways, domestic/international, wind, hydro, pumps revival, power generation
items.quote: looking ahead, we continue to see demand across key product segments, including railways and both domestic and international. In green energy, wind and hydro continue to remain strong. Pumps is showing a revival in its offtake and power generation continues to show strong demand.

items.statement: US recession risk could derail North American fleet upgrade demand for Wabtec
items.quote: if this tariff war continues, are we looking at a recession in the US And if we are, then all of those speed upgradations go away. So the biggest thing is the macro when it comes to US boils down to if there will be a recession in the US or not.

items.statement: Peak finance cost reached; net debt to reduce gradually with no major capex commitments
items.quote: There are no major capex commitments. So I think this is the peak finance cost that you can factor in. After this, you should be seeing gradual reduction.

items.statement: Targets lamination volume of 68,000-70,000 tons in current year and 72,000 tons in FY27.
items.quote: Yes, in terms of lamination volume, we are targeting about 68,000 to 70,000 tons in the current year. And for FY27, we are setting a target of 72,000, which we may upward revise going forward, looking at how the market is because to go beyond 72,000, we require capex.

items.statement: Expects 10% volume growth in domestic market once raw material prices settle.
items.quote: But once everything settles down in India regarding the price of raw material, we are expecting again a 10% volume growth in the domestic market.

items.statement: Targets 16.5-17% EBITDA margin for FY26 and a percentage point increase over next 18 months.
items.quote: Like I've said before, we should be looking at a percentage point increase in EBITDA margin over the next 18 months. For the FY26, we are looking between 16.5% to 17% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Expects net margin to grow 15-20% while revenue grows 10-12%.
items.quote: While the revenue may grow 10%, 12%, maybe around that level, your net margin should grow at maybe 15% to 20%, if not slightly higher.

items.statement: Plans INR50-60 crores machining capex in H2 and INR15 crores lamination capex this year.
items.quote: See if again, it's on a very non-committal basis, I can tell you, if the machining capacity does go up, I think that will cost us another INR50 crores to INR60 crores in H2, maybe potentially if everything is working out. In terms of lamination capacity, I really don't see anything more than INR15 crores in the current year and maybe another INR15-odd crores in the next year.

items.statement: Plans INR60-70 crores machining capex next year; cumulative INR130-140 crores over 24 months in best case.
items.quote: And for next year, in terms of machining capacity, I think it will be closer to about INR60 crores to INR70 crores, if again, everything is panning out as per plan. In the best case business scenario where you are talking about lamination volume growth beyond 72,000 and machining going to 8 lakh machine hours, cumulatively over 24 months, it will be something like INR130 crores, INR140 crores.

items.statement: Targets net debt reduction of INR100-120 crores at minimum.
items.quote: Our capex plan, which I just mentioned some time earlier, about INR50-odd crores for machine shop and about INR15 crores to INR20 crores for lamination. Despite that, I think you should look at INR 100 crore to INR 120 crore reduction in net debt at the barest minimum.

items.statement: Order book grew 8-10% from Q3 to Q4 and expected delivery grew 10% from Q4 to Q1.
items.period: Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27
items.quote: So I would say, about 8% to 10% growth in order book from Q3 to Q4. And Q4 to Q1, I would say, for real deliveries, it's flat. In terms of expected delivery, we have grown about 10% again.

items.statement: Margins unaffected in absolute terms; fixed conversion price with price variation formula for raw materials.
items.quote: So, our margins are unaffected in absolute terms. On a percentage term, it's just that inflation causes your margins to look lesser or deflation causes your margin to look better. Fixed conversion price with the customer and we have a price variation formula for raw materials, scrap and other metals such as copper, aluminium, etc.

items.statement: Raw material price increases are 100% pass-through on a quarterly mechanism.
items.quote: Balasubramanian, firstly, my industry is 100% pass-through or we don't do business. It's as simple as that. And that is something which doesn't change. It's a core tenet of the business. So, there is no question of the RM price not being passed through.

items.statement: Sees over 200% increase in RFQs, with more than 10 RFQs per month from new customers.
items.quote: Today, I would say we are getting more than 10 RFQs in a month from new customers and clients which you have never heard of. These are like medium-sized enterprises in Europe and US. They are not global names, but relatively good businesses. So that gives you an idea as to the change in profile of the buyers. In terms of absolute RFQs, I would say, there's like more than a 200% increase in RFQs.

items.statement: RFQ order sizes range from $0.5 million to $50 million annual business.
items.quote: Right from $500,000 annual business to a $50 million annual business.

items.statement: Plans to pivot product mix to more profitable machining, casting, lamination, assemblies.
items.quote: See, the thing that we are looking at internally is not to chase just volume growth, but to bring in efficiency and pivot our product mix to a more profitable eventual product mix between machining, casting, lamination, assemblies. So, the volume growth will be slow, but your margin growth will be higher.

items.statement: Cautious on tariff-driven business; focuses on fundamental competitiveness, not tariff arbitrage.
items.quote: There's going to be no third term of Trump. So, what happens after Trump goes to tariff? So we are also cautious Pulkit, in seeing to take only those businesses that without the tariff being a factor, we'll be competitive eventually globally. We don't want to take on business today only on account of tariff arbitrage.

items.statement: Aims to maintain capacity utilization around 80% and avoid bulk capexes.
items.quote: At our company level, so we would be looking at capacity utilization. We want to maintain it somewhere around 80%. Don't go in for bulk capexes like we have done in the past. The time is now to be cautiously optimistic and add capacity on a reactionary basis rather than an expectation basis.

items.statement: Projecting at least 15% volume growth for FY26
items.quote: We are projecting at least 15% volume growth from here for the next year.

items.statement: Expecting little improvement in EBITDA margin due to Chennai utilization
items.quote: There might be a little improvement in EBITDA percentage because of utilization of Chennai facility, which will reduce our overall cost, okay?

items.quote: The total investment we plan will be around INR50 crores to create a capacity of 10,000 tons of wire rope, which will generate a revenue of INR100 crores.

items.statement: Chennai facility investment of INR240 crores last year
items.quote: We have invested around INR240 crores in Chennai in last year, so -- which has increased the depreciation and also the finance cost in the numbers.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 orders for Bridgestone much higher than Q4 FY25
items.quote: Quarter 1 order for next financial year is much higher than what we sold to them in quarter 4 of last year.

items.statement: Thailand EBITDA margin target 10-11% for FY26
items.quote: I can see definitely next year, the margins would improve to about 10%, 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Chennai facility loss of INR11-12 crores in FY25, expected breakeven from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We made a loss of around INR11 crores, INR12 crores in Chennai, which has hit the bottom line by around INR11 crores.

items.statement: Indian tyre industry growth outlook 5-6%
items.quote: Current outlook remains same. There is whatever we are meeting the customers, we are getting an information that tyre will continue to grow at 5%, 6%, not beyond that.

items.statement: Chennai target 20,000 tons production in FY26 including exports
items.quote: So, we should be doing around 20,000 tons production in Chennai this year. That is the business plan we have made, okay?

items.statement: Wire rope pilot project using 12,000 tons black wire capacity at Pithampur
items.quote: So, 12,000 tons of black wire, we will now add value to that product and start making wire ropes.

items.statement: Freight saving of INR3,000-4,000 per ton from Chennai location
items.quote: Generally, there is a INR3,000 to INR4,000 saving on freight because of the location of Chennai plant, which is closer to customer and a little closer to raw material supplier also.

items.statement: US tariffs on China higher than India, positive for exports; Thailand tyre tariffs may indirectly affect after 90 days
items.quote: This U.S. tariffs have not affected us in any manner. If at all it is affected, it is a positive effect because the tariff on China is higher than tariff on India, okay, on our products.

items.statement: Chinese competition in Thailand selling at very low prices
items.quote: Currently, we are competing with -- Chinese suppliers in Thailand. And they are selling at a very low price.

items.statement: Standalone debt INR150 crores at 8-8.2% cost of funds
items.quote: Cost of fund is around 8% to 8.2%. around INR 150 crores on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: India volume grew 12% in FY25, targeting 15,000-18,000 tons growth in FY26
items.quote: Our annual business plan is for 5,000 tons growth in Thailand and around 15,000 to 18,000 tons growth in India.

items.statement: Targeting 7,000 tons additional exports from India to US and Europe in FY26
items.quote: So we are targeting 7,000 tons additional exports from Indian ports to U.S. and Europe.

items.statement: Management targets mid- to high-teen AUM growth over the medium term (3-5 years), not for FY26 specifically.
items.quote: We do want to make sure that we get to -- in the medium to long term, we do want to get to the middle teen to high-teen growth. That's our objective.

items.statement: Management aims to increase ROA to above 2% going forward, not specifically for FY26.
items.quote: We do see ourselves climbing up to 2 and beyond very soon, and there is a calibrated plan on all levels of the DuPont.

items.quote: So yes, the way to look at it in the medium -- in the next 3 to 4 years is to get the vehicle business in a mix to be closer to a 75% and the non-wheels to be 25%.

items.statement: Management guides credit cost to operate in a 1.3%-1.7% range over the medium to long term.
items.quote: I'm going to stick to a range that we would the ROA can stomach for this business. We will operate in the 1.3% to 1.7% credit cost.

items.statement: Management expects PCR to climb to 55% at the outer end over the next 4-5 quarters.

items.statement: Management believes NIMs have hit a floor at 6.5% and should climb from here due to COF benefits and pricing efficiencies.

items.statement: Confident of growth in Q1.
items.quote: in the short term on Q1, I think we are reasonably confident of getting the growth.

items.statement: Order book expected to be higher than last year.
items.quote: I am very optimistic that the order book will be higher than last year.

items.statement: Deal wins to reflect in revenue from Q1 and Q2 onwards.
items.quote: part of it should get reflected in Q1. And also spoke about sharing further update on couple of strategic deals pursuit that we are in which is what we would share in the due course, so that will start reflecting from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Manufacturing demand steady and growth oriented in short term.

items.statement: Retail has exciting strategic deals under discussion.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty persists into Q1.
items.quote: the uncertainty that was there in Q4, I don't think it has disappeared as we step into Q1, right? So it still persists in various forms and shapes.

items.quote: as the AI-led productivity starts to play out, Abhishek, we would expect that the headcount growth may not be linear with the revenue growth that we see.

items.statement: Seasonality expected to be more or less same as last year.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected around INR1,000 crores across formulation CMO, fermentation, and API production blocks
items.quote: So this year also maybe close to around INR1,000 crores capex.

items.quote: We propose to invest close to INR250 crores in the projects, which will more than double our fermentation capacity by end of 2026.

items.quote: We p lan to invest over $15 million to build a GMP facility, which will have capabilities to do plasmids, vectors, both adenovirus and lentiviral, and also ability to do antibody drug conjugation

items.quote: The growth reflects continued robust demand for our CDMO offerings and higher sales in the FDF business.

items.quote: Current facility can treat 300 patients per year, but the new facility is ready, it can treat up to 2500 patients per year.

items.quote: I think our effort is to grow faster than industry average of 5 to 7% depending on the product and category.

items.quote: No, no, it would be around Rs. 100 crore. Rs. 75 crore to 100 crore.

items.quote: But if that doesn't happen, I would say prices should only remain where they are and slightly start firming up.

items.quote: Domestic agrochemical demand is positive in terms of normal rainfall for the 2025 monsoon.

items.quote: Our ambition would be that, you know, given our brand strength, can we make a kind of a million-liter kind of product?

items.quote: Worst case scenario, China starts dumping at a cheaper price in India, but I guess , is there a possibility? The answer is yes.

items.statement: Seed business will continue to improve from current levels.
items.quote: I believe the seed will continue to improve from where we are.

items.statement: Soil and plant health business will also continue to improve.

items.statement: Domestic prices in some pockets down 5% year-on-year; cost drop passed to consumer.

items.quote: CSM business was impacted due to customer scheduling. However, long-term prospects are positive with work on new relationships .

items.statement: North cotton hybrid continues good momentum with more than a million packets sold.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments may cause short-term disruption in export market.

items.statement: Q1 CY25 EBITDA rose 55% sequentially to INR49.7 crore on better sales mix and efficiency despite lower volumes

items.statement: Gross margin expanded ~450 bps in Q1 CY25 driven by portfolio mix, operational efficiencies and cost improvements
items.quote: So it is a combination of many things, portfolio, the improvement into operational efficiencies, the cost and all. So it's a cumulative impact.

items.quote: We do have capacity, Sukhbir, and there is room that we can do more, and we are continuously working on that.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBIT margin stable at 15.3%; operating profit grew 3.9% QoQ and 11.7% YoY; FY26 margin band 14.75%-15.75% retained for investment flexibility

items.statement: Savings-Led Transformation thesis bending cost curve; clients expect AI-infused efficiency on run-the-business spend; tech spend growth only 2-3% so spends repurposed

items.quote: Logistics and Transportation and Others verticals declined sequentially by 7.7% and 3.4%, respectively. These verticals have an outsized impact by the macro environment. Nonetheless we see significant opportunities in the pipeline for both Logistics and Transportation and Healthcare.
